title: 2c — Variables

content.title: Variables are labeled boxes
content.summary: A variable holds information under a name — use that name later to get it back.
content.body: A variable is like a labeled box that holds information. You give the box a name, then put something inside it. Later, whenever you use that name, Python goes and checks what's in the box.

content.title: Creating a variable
content.summary: Use = to store a value: name = "Alex" then print(name) to display it.
content.body:
Use = to put something into a variable. The name goes on the left, and the value goes on the right.

name = "Alex"
print(name)

This stores the text "Alex" in a box called name, then prints what's inside.

content.title: You can change the value
content.summary: Assign a new value with = again at any time — that's what makes programs flexible.
content.body: Variables can be updated any time — just use = again with a new value. That's what makes programs flexible. Try changing "Alex" to your own name and run it!

editorPrompt: Create a variable, store your name in it, and print it.
progressiveHints:
# Starter code — try changing "Alex" to your name!
name = "Alex"
print(name)

# Hint: Create more variables and print them
# score = 100
# print(score)

name = "Alex"
pet = "cat"
score = 100
print(name)
print(pet)
print(score)
